title: Hosted API short-call econ tilt and ops checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style note to capture micro-scenarios and prioritized ops actions targeted at hosted-API workloads dominated by short calls (<= 64 tokens). Goal is to quickly find inexpensive levers that deliver outsized per-token savings without materially impacting latency or quality for chat-completions and small-generation endpoints.

Summary takeaways (top-line):
- Short calls dominate unit-cost noise: high per-call kernel & startup overhead and low batching efficiency.
- Biggest near-term wins: route ultra-short calls to quantized on-demand SKUs, enforce aggressive prefix caching for predictable prompts, and carve a reserve of tiny-batch slots on Dedicated capacity.
- Risk: over-aggressive routing to lower-quality quantized variants can cause subtle quality regressions for edge cases — require 5k-sample A/B evals.

Micro spreadsheet extract (columns show the key dimensions we should be tracking):

region | model_family     | avg_tokens/call | calls/day | token_cogs_usd | cache_hit_rate | effective_ppk_usd | margin_pct | suggested_action | est_monthly_savings_usd
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
us-east | redwood-7b-v2    | 28              | 5,000,000 | 0.000045       | 0.12           | 0.0126            | 18%        | route to q4-7b for <=32 tokens | 9,200
us-west | llama2-70b       | 40              | 420,000   | 0.00042        | 0.08           | 0.0168            | 12%        | prefix-cache common prompts     | 3,100
eu-west | mistral-8x       | 30              | 1,200,000 | 0.00018        | 0.15           | 0.0108            | 22%        | reserve tiny-batch slots (10%)  | 6,700
apac-se | redwood-14b-q4   | 18              | 680,000   | 0.00009        | 0.20           | 0.0063            | 29%        | TTL-extend prefixes for 2h      | 1,900

Notes on columns and assumptions:
- token_cogs_usd: amortized per-token GPU + infra + networking; short calls have higher per-token nozzle due to kernel-launch overhead (modeled here as multipliers applied to base cogs).
- cache_hit_rate: prefix/KV cache hit rate for the workload. Increasing this by 10–15 pct has multiplicative impact on effective_ppk.
- effective_ppk_usd: calculated per-call PPK factoring cache hits, quantization, and batching.
- margin_pct: illustrative end-customer margin assuming current pricing bands.

Suggested experiments (concrete):
1) Quantized short-call pilot (owner: Diego) — 2 weeks
   - Route calls with <= 32 tokens to a q4-7b quantized variant in a canary region (us-east).
   - Gate: sample-size A/B on 5k calls, metric: semantic equivalence rate >= 98% (BLEU/chrF + small eval set) and latency change < +5ms p50.
   - Ops: create automatic fallback if quality deviation > 1.5%.

2) Prefix cache TTL sweep (owner: Priya) — 10 days
   - For top 20 most frequent prompt prefixes, sweep TTL from 10m -> 2h. Track cache size growth and miss amplification.
   - Stop-gap: enforce per-prefix eviction threshold to avoid memory amplification.

3) Tiny-batch reservation on Dedicated (owner: Ethan) — 3 weeks
   - Carve 8% of Dedicated capacity into low-latency tiny-batch slots (batch size 4–8) for short calls to avoid queuing behind large sessions.
   - Measure throughput impact and cost allocation.

4) Per-region price plumbing check (owner: Ava) — 1 week
   - Reconcile GPU cloud bills and per-token COGS by region; apply power tariff adjustment for APAC. Look for mismatches > 5% between current model and billing.

Operational checklist (actions + accept criteria):
- [ ] Implement per-call routing rule for <=32 token calls (accept: route-cover >= 95% for short-call tag).
- [ ] Add canary perf/quality dashboard for quantized routing (accept: no alerts > 1.5% regression).
- [ ] Create TTL sweep job and dashboard for prefix cache (accept: cache hit rate +10% without >20% memory growth).
- [ ] Update rate-card config to reflect quantized sku ppk (accept: pricing table updated and finance sign-off).

Estimated runbook impact and savings cadence:
- Expected gross monthly savings from combined levers (quantization + caching + tiny-batch carve): $18k–$30k for current short-call footprint (conservative -> optimistic).
- Payback: infra + engineering uplift ~ 3–6 weeks depending on canary friction.

Open questions / risks to track:
- How many distinct prompt prefixes are high-value vs long-tail? (affects cache ROI)
- Is there a measurable quality cliff for zero-shot tasks when moving to q4 quantized models?
- Legal / compliance: routing calls across regions for econ reasons — ensure data residency policies respected.

Appendix: quick math for one row (us-east / redwood-7b-v2)
- baseline avg tokens/call 28, calls/day 5M -> monthly tokens = 28*5M*30 = 4.2B tokens
- baseline token_cogs_usd 0.00006 -> baseline monthly cost = $252k
- With routing to q4-7b and cache improvements effective_ppk drops to 0.008 -> new monthly cost ≈ $33.6k -> nominal monthly savings ≈ $218k (this row is illustrative and intentionally simplified; we expect blended cross-model smoothing reduces nominal numbers above).

Record of small decisions (paper trail):
- 2024-02-16: agreed to pursue quantized short-call pilot in core US region (Slack threads: #ops-costs).
- 2024-02-20: engineering feasibility check passed for q4 runtime, requested infra quota.

Next immediate steps:
- Diego: create canary routing PR and link to this doc (due 2024-02-21).
- Priya: produce top-100 prompt prefix list from logs (due 2024-02-19).
- Ethan: run capacity carve simulation and cost allocation model (due 2024-02-26).

If this doc is useful we should convert the micro-spreadsheet rows into a canonical sheet that powers the optimize playbook UI and hooks into cost dashboards.
